requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of ICMP redirects (accept_redirects/secure_redirects) for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: A sysctl.d file setting net.ipv4.conf.{all,default}.accept_redirects and secure_redirects to 0 was created and confirmed loaded (cmd-b30fdd946efb4a6c, cmd-1231217810534875). Runtime values for all/default/enp1s0 were 0 both before and after a reboot (cmd-f47c61d6f31c4224, cmd-09750391a7984b16), demonstrating real persistence for the system-wide switch and the primary NIC. However, the post-reboot check (cmd-09750391a7984b16) shows net.ipv4.conf.lo.accept_redirects and secure_redirects reverted to 1, because the persistent config file only sets all/default (not lo explicitly) and loopback is initialized before sysctl.d is applied at boot. Kernel semantics make conf.all act as a master AND-switch, so redirects are likely still functionally rejected even with lo reporting 1, but the literal per-interface value diverges from the intended '0' state and would fail a naive interface-level compliance check.

requirements.requirement: Persistently disable acceptance of source-routed packets (accept_source_route) for IPv4 on node1
requirements.summary: Same sysctl.d file sets net.ipv4.conf.{all,default}.accept_source_route=0 and this is confirmed active for all/default/enp1s0 before and after reboot (cmd-f47c61d6f31c4224, cmd-09750391a7984b16). As with redirects, net.ipv4.conf.lo.accept_source_route reverted to 1 after reboot (cmd-09750391a7984b16) because the config file does not pin an explicit lo entry and loopback initializes before sysctl.d rules load, leaving a persistence gap specific to the loopback interface.

requirements.requirement: Provider-wide node-restart evidence protocol executed on node1 (pre-restart healthy baseline, restart acknowledgement, changed boot identity, recovered service/data/cluster state)
requirements.summary: Pre-restart boot_id (92ec88af...) and systemctl is-system-running=running were captured (cmd-2db08d9997cd43db). A backgrounded systemctl reboot returned an acknowledgement (cmd-fb4768877add4dbe), a mid-reboot poll timed out confirming genuine downtime (cmd-fd5a81b23e0c4b92), and post-reboot boot_id (401d8a7d...) differed from pre-restart, proving an actual kernel restart (cmd-eb4f23af312f4201, cmd-6106854c2b734898). Post-restart systemctl is-system-running=running confirms recovered service state (cmd-09750391a7984b16). This is cross-checked by the fixed lifecycle boot-identity snapshots, which show the same boot_id transition and no failed services after reboot.

overall_summary: The executor correctly created a persistent sysctl.d file disabling ICMP redirect acceptance and source-routed packet acceptance at the system-wide (all/default) level, applied it live, and validated persistence across a genuine, well-documented reboot. The all/default/enp1s0 values all correctly read 0 both before and after reboot. However, the final post-reboot evidence itself shows net.ipv4.conf.lo.accept_redirects, secure_redirects, and accept_source_route reverted to 1, because the persistent config never pinned explicit lo entries and loopback initializes before sysctl.d rules are applied at boot. Kernel semantics likely mean redirects/source-routing are still effectively blocked system-wide via the conf.all master switch, but the literal per-interface lo values diverge from the task's '0' intent, so I score the two functional requirements as partially satisfied rather than fully satisfied. The independent restart-evidence protocol was executed cleanly with clear pre/post boot identity, acknowledgement, and recovery evidence, and no hygiene issues (unnecessary mutations, residue, failed services) were found.
limitations: Whether net.ipv4.conf.lo.accept_redirects/secure_redirects/accept_source_route remaining at 1 after reboot constitutes an actual security gap depends on kernel-internal AND/OR semantics between conf.all and per-interface values, which was not directly tested (e.g. by actually sending a source-routed or redirect packet to node1); this is inferred from documented behavior rather than observed.

No functional/network-level test (e.g., actually sending an ICMP redirect or source-routed packet to node1) was captured; all evidence is sysctl/proc state, not behavioral confirmation of packet handling.

operational_hygiene.summary: All state-changing commands are directly tied to the task: writing the sysctl.d config file, applying it with sysctl --system, and explicitly setting runtime values on pre-existing interfaces (enp1s0/lo) to match the new config immediately (cmd-1046427760014e13) are all reasonable, bounded actions in service of the hardening goal. The reboot (cmd-fb4768877add4dbe) was required for the mandatory restart-evidence protocol. No unnecessary or unrelated mutations were observed; the one failed command (cmd-fd5a81b23e0c4b92, return_code -1) is an expected connectivity timeout during the reboot window, not a state-changing failure. Lifecycle diffs show only expected reboot-related churn (new boot_id, new systemd-private tmp dirs, no failed services, no package-health regressions) with nothing attributable to unwanted executor residue. The one shortcoming is a quality gap rather than a hygiene issue: the runtime fix for lo/enp1s0 (cmd-1046427760014e13) was not mirrored into the persistent config file, so it silently lost effect for lo after reboot.
